evidence: test_t5c_grounding.py:43-51 assert exact prose fragments: `assert "GROUNDING OVERRIDE (this criterion only)" in text` / `assert "FLIPS a finding" in text`
test_t5c_grounding.py:61-67 pins wording `assert "demoted, never suppressed" in text` and `assert "neither a repo artifact you actually read" in text`

passes.py:227-232: rubric files `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_*.md` are the LLM pass system prompts, resolved via the prompt machinery and fed to the finder — an LLM consumer, which the standard states is NOT a non-human consumer of a grepped token
Litmus: a behavior-preserving reword of the T5c rubric (same instruction, different phrasing) would fail these assertions with zero change to review behavior
advisory.finding: The new test module test_t5c_grounding.py consists entirely of exact-substring assertions over the plan_review_T5c.md rubric PROSE (e.g. "FLIPS a finding", "demoted, never suppressed", "neither a repo artifact you actually read", "ground the plan's security implications in the CURRENT codebase and configuration via the read tools"). The rubric .md is loaded verbatim and rendered into the LLM finder prompt (passes.py:227-232), so these tokens are consumed by an LLM, not by any parser/validator that branches on their exact value. Per the test standard an LLM is not a non-human consumer, so these are change-detectors on author wording: any behavior-preserving reword of the rubric breaks the tests without any observable-behavior change (refactoring-violation criterion).
advisory.suggested_fix: Restrict the pins to genuinely canonical tokens that a downstream consumer keys on (e.g. the criterion id and the two HIGH-class names), and drop the free-prose fragment assertions; where the change's intent is behavioral (severity scoping keeps lesser findings below the 0.90 bar), assert it through the Pass-3 pipeline as test_criteria_blocking.py already does rather than via rubric text.
